what: [R/sd_ci_timepoint.R:24-26] CI→SD conversion is ~2.5× too large (missing factor of 2, wrong t quantile)
title: HDXBoxeR — bug worklist (branch correlation_V2)
text: Bug: cited source (Cochrane 7.7.3.2, roxygen block) gives SE = (UL - LL) / (2 * t_{1-alpha/2, df}) SD = SE * sqrt(N). code omits factor 2 uses qt(alpha, ...) (one-tailed quantile) two-sided t.test(conf.level = 1-alpha) interval requires qt(alpha/2, ...). Evidence: alpha = 0.01, replicates = 3: code uses t = |qt(0.01,4)| = 3.747, correct 2 * |qt(0.005,4)| = 2 * 4.604 = 9.21. Ratio = 2.46× overestimate. Impact: sd_ci_timepoint() default SD source plot_fissure_vent() (sd_source = "CI"). Every uncertainty ellipse ~2.5× big global CI band derived SDs (CI_2pts) ~2.5× wide, significant peptides -called. statistical-correctness bug, cosmetic. Suggested fix: (Also consider using tt$parameter, Welch df, rather replicates*2-2.) Update formula roxygen block plot_fissure_vent.R’s @details, repeat wrong formula.
code: tvalue=abs(qt(alpha, replicates*2-2))                     # line 24: should be alpha/2 tt<-t.test(x1, x2, conf.level = c(1-alpha))               # two-sided interval sd.ci<-(tt$conf.int[2]-tt$conf.int[1])/tvalue*sqrt(replicates)   # line 26: missing /2 tvalue <- abs(qt(alpha/2, replicates*2-2)) sd.ci  <- (tt$conf.int[2]-tt$conf.int[1]) / (2*tvalue) * sqrt(replicates)

what: [R/residue_deconvolution.R:76-82] peptide_exch_residues() includes one residue too many — contradicts nb_exch_deut()
title: HDXBoxeR — bug worklist (branch correlation_V2)
text: Bug: roxygen says helper matches nb_exch_deut()’s convention (“first residue peptide Prolines excluded”). nb_exch_deut() actually excludes first two residues: (End-Start) - nP + firstP - 1 = L - 2 - nP_after_first. helper starts local index 2, giving L - 1 - nP_after_first — one extra residue per peptide. Evidence: vs R/nb_exchangeable_protons.R:15-16: [reproduced] 128 peptides shipped example, length(peptide_exch_residues(...)) - nb_exch_deut(...) == 1 (every single row). Impact: design matrix spreads peptide’s observed uptake one extra residue, every per-residue estimate systematically diluted peptide’s N-terminal shoulder, residue Start+1 (rest package treats non-exchangeable) assigned spurious value. Also breaks vignette’s cross-validation section, copy-pastes helper (vignettes/HDXBoxeR.Rmd, “Choosing lambda_smooth”) — CV fit scored --one detect . Suggested fix: mirror change vignette chunk. Better: factor helper real (possibly non-exported) function nb_exch_deut(), deconvolution, vignette share one definition — length(peptide_exch_residues(...)) == nb_exch_deut(...) natural unit test.
code: peptide_exch_residues <- function(start, seq_string) {   chars <- strsplit(seq_string, "")[[1]]   if (length(chars) < 2) return(integer(0))   local_idx <- 2:length(chars)                 # <- line 79, should be 3:length(chars)   resid_idx <- start + local_idx - 1   resid_idx[chars[local_idx] != "P"] } nb_exch_deut<-c(c(df$End-df$Start)-str_count(df$Sequence,'P') ) +   as.numeric(substr(df$Sequence, 1, 1)=="P")-1 if (length(chars) < 3) return(integer(0)) local_idx <- 3:length(chars)

Tools > Options > Display > Deuteration Table: Display columns (select show low-confidence results). 4. Tools > Export > results table. title: HDXBoxeR
text: HDXBoxeR employs hybrid statistical approach using Welch T-test Critical interval statistical framework proposed Hageman Weis (Hageman Weis; Anal. Chem. 2019, 91, 13, 8008–8016). deemed significantly different, peptides must meet significance criteria individual peptide level (Welch T-test) surpass global critical interval peptides set. detailed information, please refer cited paper (Hageman Weis; Anal. Chem. 2019, 91, 13, 8008–8016). short, Welch T-test determines Null hypothesis can rejected (Null hypothesis: average two means individual peptides equal). individual critical interval p-value, null hypothesis rejected – peptides deemed significant individual peptide standpoint. global significance threshold, propagated standard error pooled standard deviation means peptides two sets calculated scaled Student distribution. involves calculating pooled standard deviation two sets separately, propagating error overall standard deviation two sets, finally, scaling T-distribution determine global critical interval global threshold. peptides passed criteria whole set individual peptides, deemed significant. plot_fissure_vent() shows hybrid criterion geometrically - state1 vs state2 deuteration plotted directly (delta column), global critical interval drawn bands parallel diagonal peptide’s Welch test drawn ellipse calibrated touching diagonal means peptide’s p-value clear cutoff. what: 7. Summary Information Generation about Data Sets
title: HDXBoxeR
text: HDXBoxeR functionality return summary information sets, including timepoints, number replicates, number peptides, peptide coverage, average peptide length, average redundancy, standard deviation, critical interval, average back exchange, back exchange range. information provided complies Masson et al., Nature Methods volume 16, pages 595–602 (2019). all_summary() function requires undeuterated fully deuterated sets marked Deut.time 0s FD, respectively. Also, calculation back exchange, Dfact parameter needs specified. Here the times in seconds x<-c(4, 60,1800, 72000) #par(mfrow=c(1,2)) uptake_plots(tc_aP[1:2,],x)   # Boxplots boxplot_tp(a, col= c("gold2", "dodgerblue"))  # Volcano plots plots_vol_tp(a, col=c(2,3), replicates=3, pvalue = 0.01)  # Significantly different peptides plot across the sequence #par(mfrow=c(4,1)) # uncomment to have 4 panels plot_peptide_sig_tp(a,nb_pep_row = 18, ranges = c(-Inf, -10, -2.5,0,2.5, 10, Inf), pvalue = 0.01)   ##Average uptake heat maps ### heat maps  plot_heat_map_tp(a, mar_x=8, ranges = c(-Inf, -10, -2.5,0,2.5, 10, Inf), pvalue=0.01)  ### heat map for procent deuteration, require both uptake and procent deuteration data frame as input plot_heat_map_tp_proc(input_up = a, input_proc = b, replicates=3)  ###Maximum uptake or procent deuteration per peptide plot_heat_map_max_uptake_tp(a, replicates=3) ###  plot_heat_map_max_uptake_tp_proc(input_up = a, input_proc = b, replicates=3, mar_x=8, ranges = c(-Inf, -10, -2.5,0,2.5, 10, Inf), pvalue=0.01)  ## Legend for the heatmaps. #default ranges for figures does not require argument legend_heat_map(ranges = c(-Inf, -10, -2.5,0,2.5, 10, Inf))  ###################### ###Timecourses plots ######################  ## average procent deuteration in timecourse plots_av_tcourse(tc_aP, replicates = 3) ###average heat map for timecourses plot_heat_map_tc(tc_aP, replicates=3) legend_heat_map_timecourse()  ###Robot plots for the timecourses robot_plot_All(thP = tc_aP, th=tc_a, pvalue=0.01)  ##############Woods plots ##timecourse and timepoint woods plots ################  indp<-select_indices(b,  times = c("3.00s", "60.00s")) deuteration_woods_timepoints(b[indp,], replicates = 3)  ## input for timecourses  deuteration_woods_timecourse(tc_aP, replicates=3)  ###woods plots woods_CI_plot(thP = tc_aP, th=tc_a) ###Use more stringent parameters to have fewer peptides drawn: lower pvalue and alpha (critical interval). woods_CI_plot(thP = tc_aP, th=tc_a, pvalue=0.005, alpha = 0.001)   ####################### ##Pymol scripts #######################  pymol_script_significant_peptide(a, path=tempdir(), ranges=c(-Inf, seq(-120, 120, by=10), Inf), pvalue = 0.01,replicates = 3) ###same but for percent deuteration pymol_script_significant_peptide_proc(input_proc = b, input_up = a,path=tempdir(), ranges=c(-Inf, seq(-120, 120, by=10), Inf), pvalue = 0.01,replicates = 3, order.pep=FALSE)  ###scripts prepared by residue pymol_script_significant_residue(a, path=tempdir(), ranges=c(-Inf, seq(-120, 120, by=10), Inf), pvalue = 0.01,replicates = 3)  ################## ##Summary ################## all_summary(file_nm, Dfact=0.85,replicates = 3)  ############### ##Outputs ###############  ###final output for the paper  ### USAGE output_prep(pathto_allresults.csv, output_name.csv) output_prep(filepath = file_nm, output_name = tempfile())  ###long version of the uptake data, timepoint ### USAGE output_tp_csv(pathto_allresults.csv, output_name.csv) output_tp(filepath =file_nm , csv = tempfile())  ### verbose versions of the output functions create csv files with all important data averages, sd, and pvalues for uptake data verbose_timepoint_output(filepath = file_nm, output_name = tempfile(), percent=TRUE)  ########################### ##Extreme input preparation ###########################  # returns empty column if data is missing extreme_input_gap(hm_dir ="filepath", replicates = 3,                    timepoints =c(3, 60, 1800, 72000), output_path=tempdir()) # if data is missing, it writes there values for undeuterated  extreme_input_undeut(hm_dir ="filepath", replicates = 2,                      timepoints =c(3, 60, 1800, 72000), output_path=tempdir())

title: Data Quality: Coverage, Redundancy, and Back-Exchange
text: general_info() gives, per state, number peptides, sequence coverage, average peptide length, redundancy (many peptides cover average residue): Low coverage means part sequence measured. significant difference means “measured”, “change”. Low redundancy means residue covered peptides, one bad peptide cross-checked. backHX_calculations() gives back-exchange per state. uses undeuterated (0s) fully deuterated (FD) controls, measured centroids (m/z x charge): different back-exchange states can bias comparison.
code: general_info(file_nm) #>         Protein.State                      Timepoints # replicates # peptides #> Unbound       Unbound 3.00s 60.00s 1800.00s 72000.00s            3         37 #> bound           bound 3.00s 60.00s 1800.00s 72000.00s            3         34 #>         peptide coverage % <Peptide Length> <Redundancy> #> Unbound              94.09            13.86         2.93 #> bound                94.09            13.29         2.58 backHX_calculations(file_nm) #>         <BackHX> BackHX Range From    To #> Unbound    27.01              1.31 51.48 #> bound      35.44             11.73 99.88 #> attr(,"method") #> [1] "measured centroid (Exp Cent) x Charge: 1 - (m_FD - m_0s)/N/Dfact"

code: library(HDXBoxeR) file_nm <- system.file("extdata", "All_results_table.csv", package = "HDXBoxeR") a <- output_tp(file_nm, percent = TRUE) #> Protein.States used: Unbound bound #> Deut.times used: 3.00s 60.00s 1800.00s 72000.00s #> 29 peptide row(s) dropped: 29 not measured in every state, 0 with fewer than 2 replicate value(s) #> Number of replicates used: Unbound=3 bound=3 #> no csv file written res <- residue_level_average(a, protein_length = 225) pdb_demo <- system.file("examples", "1hel.pdb", package = "bio3d") plot_hdx_structure(res, pdb = pdb_demo, state1 = "Unbound", state2 = "bound",                    times = "1800.00s", chain = "A") res_1800 <- res[res$Deut.Time == "1800.00s", ] delta <- rowMeans(res_1800[, grep("^bound", colnames(res_1800))], na.rm = TRUE) -   rowMeans(res_1800[, grep("^Unbound", colnames(res_1800))], na.rm = TRUE) step <- max(abs(delta), na.rm = TRUE) / 3 plot_hdx_structure_legend(c(-Inf, -3*step, -2*step, -step, 0, step, 2*step, 3*step, Inf),                           unit_label = "% Deut")

text: HDXBoxeR analyses hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS) data: exported peptide table statistically tested differences protein states, publication tables, figures structure-coloring scripts.

title: Analysis of Hydrogen-Deuterium Exchange Mass-Spectrometry Data
text: Reads HDXExaminer “results” tables Waters DynamX cluster/state exports (read_hdx()), long table (as_hdx_long()). States may different numbers replicates, missing replicates handled. Tests differences states one rule throughout - Welch t-test p-value pooled critical interval Hageman & Weis (2019) - optional false-discovery-rate correction (p_adjust = "BH") length-normalized values (percent = "per_residue"). Compares two states peptide peptide (plot_fissure_vent(), volcano, Woods, heat maps, robot plots), three states (compare_states_tp()), whole regions (compare_regions(), region ANOVA peptides controls), whole time courses (compare_timecourse()), states different peptide maps (compare_states_unmatched()), finds contiguous affected regions (residue_regions()). Checks data quality: coverage, redundancy, back-exchange, peptide-level flags (peptide_qc(), plot_peptide_coverage_map()). Normalizes fully deuterated control (percent = "FD"). Reports: summary table recommended Masson et al. (2019) (hdx_summary_table()), tidy results table parameters (hdx_results_table()), publication-format data (output_prep()), one-command HTML report (render_report()). Visualizes structures: PyMOL scripts interactive NGL views (plot_hdx_structure()), plus linked interactive plots (interactive_fissure_explorer()).

text: t-value two-tailed, |qt(alpha/2, df)|, published version package. text: Every significance function package (plot_fissure_vent(), diff_peptides_prep(), robot_indexes()) compares exactly two states time. function two things three states: (1) omnibus test per peptide across requested states (peptide differ across ) - default Welch one-way ANOVA (stats::oneway.test(), unequal variances), reported used gate significance (see Details) - (2) package's usual Hageman & Weis hybrid test (pooled CI_2pts() + per-pair Welch p-value) every pair states (every reference vs. rest, reference given). pair significant Welch p-value (raw default, adjusted p_adjust across peptides pair) pvalue difference exceeds pooled CI - rule every function package.

code: compare_states_tp(   filepath,   times,   states = NULL,   by = c("sequence", "position"),   reference = NULL,   regions = NULL,   replicates = NULL,   alpha = 0.01,   pvalue = 0.01,   p_adjust = "none",   omnibus = c("welch", "kruskal"),   percent = FALSE,   p_adjust_method )

title: Compare peptide-level HDX uptake across three or more protein states — compare_states_tp
text: filepath filepath input file (format output_tp()/nm_states() expect) - function calls output_tp() internally, per pair plus states together, rather taking already-built wide table, precisely wide format already discarded availability information available-case matching needs (see Details). times single Deut.Time value compare . states character vector three states compare. Default NULL uses every state found filepath (nm_states()). matching rule identifying "peptide" across states. "sequence" (default) requires identical Sequence, Start, End Charge states (output_tp()'s seq_match = FALSE). "position" matches Start, End Charge , ignoring Sequence (output_tp()'s seq_match = TRUE), peptide covering point mutation still compared; Sequence reported per-state sequences joined ".". modes peptide_id Start_End_zCharge (plus sequence "sequence" mode), charge state peptide. reference optional state name. given, reference vs. state tested (N-1 pairs, Dunnett-style), instead every pair (N(N-1)/2) - fewer simultaneous tests usually actually-relevant contrast wild-type/apo vs. several perturbations design. Default NULL tests every pair. regions optional named list c(start, end) residue ranges (e.g. list(NTR = c(1, 85), ACD = c(86, 165))). supplied, peptides fully contained region (Start >= start & End <= end) compared, run separately per region, result gets region column. Default NULL compares every peptide filtering (region column output). replicates optional maximum number replicates per state (passed output_tp()). Default NULL uses every replicate; states may differ. alpha alpha pooled critical interval (CI_2pts()), applied per pair. Default 0.01. pvalue significance cutoff applied per-pair p-value (raw, adjusted p_adjust). Default 0.01. p_adjust multiple-testing correction passed stats::p.adjust(): "none" (default, raw Welch p-values, every function) e.g. "BH". Pairwise p-values adjusted across peptides pair states (family everywhere package); omnibus p-values adjusted across peptides. omnibus omnibus test across states per peptide: "welch" (default, Welch one-way ANOVA) "kruskal" (Kruskal-Wallis). percent passed output_tp() - FALSE (default) compares uptake Daltons, TRUE percent deuteration, "FD" percent fully deuterated control, "per_residue" uptake per exchangeable amide (removes peptide length critical-interval condition). p_adjust_method deprecated; earlier versions adjusted p_adjust_method = "BH" default. Supplying sets p_adjust, warning.

text: value: filepath's raw # Deut column (Da uptake, read X..Deut) used directly default (value = "raw") - per-peptide size correction kind. Two options exist, default: "raw" Default. Raw deuterium uptake Da, exactly # Deut column input file - direct reading data, compare_states_tp()/plot_fissure_vent()/diff_peptides_prep() use well (percent = FALSE default). "percent" HDX Examiner's Deut % column - uptake already expressed relative peptide's theoretical maximum. "frac_deut" package's derived metric: # Deut divided peptide's number exchangeable protons (see nb_exch_deut()) - finer-grained per-residue normalization "percent". Useful specifically pooling peptides different lengths together one region length difference otherwise dominate pooled comparison (longer peptide mechanically carries larger raw Da value regardless intrinsic exchange rate) - trades normalizing away part signal, opt-, default. per-peptide p-values depend choice (dividing one peptide's two states constant change t-test's p-value), critical-interval half per-peptide rule pooled result (shift_hl/p_value/p_omnibus, pools values across different peptides) computed chosen scale.

title: Compare pooled peptide-level HDX uptake across states without matching peptides — compare_states_unmatched
text: "peptide" (default) peptide contributes one value per state (replicates averaged first). Recommended default - avoids replicate pseudo-replication (replicates one peptide independent draws "state exchanges"). Omnibus: Kruskal-Wallis. Pairwise: Wilcoxon rank-sum, reported alongside Hodges-Lehmann shift estimate. "classic" Pools every replicate row observation (replicates x n_peptides points per state) - reproduces pooling package's prior ad hoc analyses used. Triggers warning: replicates within peptide highly correlated, inflates effective sample size understates p-values. Kept reproducing prior results, recommended new analyses. "resample" Peptide-level like "peptide", p-values come label-permutation test (permuting peptide belongs state recomputing test statistic) rather Kruskal-Wallis/Wilcoxon asymptotic approximation, pairwise shift_hl gets percentile bootstrap confidence interval (resampling peptides replacement within state). Slower (n_perm + n_boot resamples per pair/region); defensible small peptide counts per state asymptotic tests unreliable.

title: Summary table for HDX-MS reporting (Masson et al. 2019) — hdx_summary_table
text: Builds summary table recommended Masson et al. (2019, Nat Methods 16:595) publishing HDX-MS data: one row per item, one column per protein state. Items computed data: time course, controls, replicates, number peptides, sequence coverage, average peptide length, redundancy, back-exchange (mean range), repeatability (pooled replicate SD, Da) significance threshold: critical interval used state compared first state (values hdx_results_table()). Items know (labeling buffer, pH, temperature, quench, protease, LC/MS, software ...) added metadata.

title: Interactive Woods plot, linked to the volcano/fissure_vent/table views — interactive_woods
text: df output output_tp(). state1 First protein state, matched plot_fissure_vent(). Defaults first state found df. state2 Second protein state. Defaults second state found. times single Deut.Time value plot. replicates number replicates. Default 3. alpha alpha pooled critical interval. Default 0.01. May vector (paired element-wise pvalue, recycled common length) - one combination, plot gets dropdown (native plotly updatemenus, R session needed) swaps pre-computed colorings/thresholds alpha/pvalue pair. Peptide positions never move (delta p-value depend either parameter) - points/lines count significant. pvalue per-peptide significance cutoff. Default 0.01. See alpha vector/dropdown behavior. shared_data optional crosstalk::SharedData object (built internally interactive_fissure_explorer()) plot's selection linked plots sharing object. text: filepath filepath input file. Input file All_results table HDX_Examiner, fields marked export. Can also DynamX cluster/state export, table read_hdx() / as_hdx_long(). replicates optional maximum number replicates per state time. default every replicate used; missing measurements NA. Replicates numbered order experiments appear file. states function allows choose states used analysis. Default states used. times lists deuteration times used analysis. Default states used. seq_match peptides matched time points, output_tp(). FALSE (default): Sequence, Start, End Charge. TRUE: matched position , ignoring Sequence; differing sequences joined ".". csv Flag allowing saving output csv. default csv="NA", data saved. csv output desided, provide output name. percent values . FALSE (default): deuterium uptake Da. TRUE: percent deuteration reported input (HDXExaminer's Deut %, .e. relative theoretical maximum; DynamX 100 x uptake / MaxUptake). "FD": percent measured fully deuterated control, 100 x uptake / FD uptake peptide state (FD replicates averaged, charge states pooled); corrects back-exchange D2O content. Peptides without usable FD value (missing, FD uptake <= 0) keep row empty (NA) values. "per_residue": uptake per exchangeable amide, Da / nb_exch_deut() (length - 2 - prolines first residue), peptide length affect critical-interval half significance rule (TRUE "FD" length-normalized ). p-values every scale; critical interval differences change. min_replicates peptide kept state least many replicate values every time. Default 2.

text: filepath filepath input file. Input file All_results table HDX_Examiner, fields marked export. Can also DynamX cluster/state export, table read_hdx() / as_hdx_long(). replicates optional maximum number replicates per state time. default every replicate used, states may different numbers replicates (e.g. 3 4); missing measurements NA. Replicates numbered order experiments appear file. states function allows choose states used analysis. Default states used. times lists deuteration times used analysis. Default states used. seq_match peptides matched states. FALSE (default): peptide kept Sequence, Start, End Charge found every state (exact sequence identity). TRUE: peptides matched position (Start, End Charge), ignoring Sequence, peptides covering e.g. point mutation kept; sequences differ states joined "." Sequence column. csv Flag allowing saving output csv. default csv="NA", data saved. csv output desided, provide output name. percent values . FALSE (default): deuterium uptake Da. TRUE: percent deuteration reported input (HDXExaminer's Deut %, .e. relative theoretical maximum; DynamX 100 x uptake / MaxUptake). "FD": percent measured fully deuterated control, 100 x uptake / FD uptake peptide state (FD replicates averaged, charge states pooled); corrects back-exchange D2O content. Peptides without usable FD value (missing, FD uptake <= 0) keep row empty (NA) values. "per_residue": uptake per exchangeable amide, Da / nb_exch_deut() (length - 2 - prolines first residue), peptide length affect critical-interval half significance rule (TRUE "FD" length-normalized ). p-values every scale; critical interval differences change. min_replicates peptide kept least many replicate values every state time. Default 2, minimum standard deviation t-test. .arg_df advanced/internal: pre-computed arg_df() data.frame filepath, skip re-reading re-parsing file disk. Default NULL reads filepath usual - pass calling output_tp() many times file (e.g. per pair states) arg_df(filepath) already computed caller; passing data.frame match filepath silently produce wrong results, since nothing re-checks .

title: Per-residue deconvolution of HDX-MS uptake from overlapping peptides — residue_deconvolution
text: Estimates single-residue-resolution deuterium uptake profile overlapping peptide-level data, solving constrained least-squares problem rather simply averaging peptides cover residue. peptide's observed uptake (Daltons) modelled sum per-residue uptake every exchangeable residue covers (first two residues peptide non-first Prolines excluded, matching convention used nb_exch_deut()). resulting system solved per Protein State, replicate, timepoint residue-level uptake constrained \[0, 1\] (residue less fully protected fully deuterated). typical overlapping-peptide coverage (redundancy > ~5x), recovers sharper, localized residue-level resolution plain per-residue mean across covering peptides, particularly region boundaries long peptides otherwise blend signal neighboring residues region's apparent value.

title: Per-residue deconvolution of HDX-MS uptake from overlapping peptides — residue_deconvolution

title: Per-residue deconvolution of HDX-MS uptake from overlapping peptides — residue_deconvolution
text: df data.frame, output output_tp() called percent = FALSE. Uptake Daltons required additive across residues; percent deuteration (depends peptide's number exchangeable residues) used directly deconvolution. protein_length integer, total number residues protein. Used set residue index range deconvolution. lambda_smooth non-negative numeric, default 0.1. Strength L2 penalty difference adjacent covered residues (applied residues actually consecutive sequence - gap coverage breaks chain). 0 reproduces original, unregularized per-timepoint fit. Larger values pull neighboring residues toward value unless peptide data specifically distinguish . default 0.1 modest starting point, universally correct value - right strength depends peptide redundancy protein size. example data, values 0 1 predicted left-peptides equally well.

title: HDXBoxeR 0.1.0
text: plot_fissure_vent(): state 1 vs state 2 deuteration plot per-peptide Welch confidence ellipses (ellipse touching diagonal means peptide’s p-value cutoff) pooled Hageman & Weis critical-interval band. Interactive, linked views: interactive_volcano(), interactive_fissure_vent(), interactive_woods(), interactive_fissure_explorer() (plotly/crosstalk). Multi-state comparisons: compare_states_tp() (three states, Welch ANOVA omnibus plus pairwise hybrid tests, optional BH correction; = "sequence" = "position" peptide matching) compare_states_unmatched() (region-level comparison peptide maps differ states, per-peptide diagnostic), plot_compare_states_tp(), plot_compare_states_unmatched() plot_coverage_diagnostics(). Per-residue analysis: residue_deconvolution(), residue_level_average(), residue_regions(), residue_regions_subset_summary(). Structure mapping: plot_hdx_structure(), plot_hdx_structure_legend(). Data quality: plot_peptide_coverage_map(); long-format helpers boxer_input_to_long() all_data_long_input(). New vignettes: fissure vent, interactive explorer, multi-state (anova), structure mapping, data quality. unfinished correlation-plots vignette removed.

title: HDXBoxeR 0.1.0
text: Argument names consistent: pvalue (pv_cutoff) col (cola / colors_initial). old names still work, deprecation warning. 0.0.2, pv_cutoff sets p-value cutoff critical-interval alpha (unless alpha given). plotting PyMOL functions now separate alpha pvalue arguments, placed pv_cutoff . Calls pass values position (e.g. plot_heat_map_tp(, 3.5, ranges, 0.05, 3)) now set different arguments: name arguments. CI_factor removed robot Woods plot functions; use alpha. PyMOL script functions gain resno_offset match structure numbering. Internal helper functions marked internal (still exported; hidden help index). _proc functions documented percent-deuteration counterparts uptake versions (significance uptake, differences shown percent deuteration). New example data three_states.csv (wild type two point mutants, uneven replicates; Woods et al. 2025, PNAS). New vignette("input_formats"); README rewritten; pkgdown reference grouped task; main vignette shows summary/output code points newer tools; stale references removed functions fixed.

title: HDXBoxeR 0.1.0
text: New render_report(): one-command HTML report analysis parameters, summary table, data-quality checks, significant-peptide counts fissure-vent plots per time point, optionally region ANOVAs whole-time-course results; tidy results table written next . computed items (time course, controls, replicates, peptides, coverage, length, redundancy, back-exchange, repeatability, significance threshold) plus experimental details via metadata; csv markdown. New hdx_results_table(): tidy per-peptide, per-time, per-pair results (means, SDs, n, difference, p-value, adjusted p-value, CI, call), written csv _parameters.txt file holding parameters sessionInfo(). Results compare_states_tp(), compare_states_unmatched(), compare_regions(), compare_timecourse(), residue_regions(), plot_fissure_vent() new tables carry parameters, package version date attribute "hdxboxer". compare_states_unmatched() gains seed reproducible resampling. output_prep(): Mean.Peptide_Mass_[Da] now measured neutral peptide mass (Charge x (centroid m/z - proton mass)); previously held centroid m/z. percent column labelled [%] instead [Da], column names longer mangled (_[Da] instead _.Da.), table returned invisibly. general_info()/all_summary(): average peptide length counts residues (End - Start + 1); one residue short.

what: Statistics: one significance rule, regions and time courses
title: HDXBoxeR 0.1.0
text: One significance rule everywhere: peptide differs Welch p-value pvalue difference exceeds pooled critical interval. p-values raw default; every function calls significance now takes p_adjust (e.g. "BH"), including pv_timepoint(), pv_timecourse(), heat map, volcano, Woods, robot peptide plots, PyMOL scripts, plot_fissure_vent(), interactive plots, diff_peptides_prep() verbose_timepoint_output(). compare_states_tp(): raw p-values default (p_adjust = "none"; previously BH) Welch one-way ANOVA reported omnibus test (omnibus = "kruskal" previous Kruskal-Wallis test). p_adjust_method deprecated. peptide two overlapping regions now enters multiple-testing correction . residue_regions(): peptides called package-wide rule (previously BH-adjusted p < fdr_cutoff critical interval; fdr_cutoff still works, deprecated, reproduces rule). Charge states one peptide count towards min_peptides, per-residue effect difference per exchangeable amide. compare_states_unmatched(): per-peptide diagnostic uses package-wide rule, listed first summary, per-peptide results returned peptides; pooled test documented approximate. p_adjust replaces p_adjust_method (default now "none"). New compare_regions(): region-level two-way ANOVA (peptide + state) matched peptides, peptide control; pairwise state contrasts, state x peptide heterogeneity test, optional model time points state x time test. New compare_timecourse(): per-peptide summed difference time course global critical interval, number time points peptide significant. robot_indexes(), robot_indexes_df() robot_plot_All() gain min_timepoints. New percent = "per_residue" output_tp()/output_tc(): uptake per exchangeable amide, peptide length affect critical-interval half rule. plot_fissure_vent() returns (invisibly) table drew. multi-state vignette now vignette("multistate").

what: Fully deuterated control and quality checks
title: HDXBoxeR 0.1.0
text: output_tp()/output_tc() gain percent = "FD": percent measured fully deuterated control, 100 * uptake / FD uptake peptide state (FD replicates averaged, charge states pooled), corrects back-exchange D2O content. Peptides without usable FD value (missing, FD uptake <= 0) keep row empty (NA) values. percent = TRUE still returns input’s percent deuteration (HDXExaminer Deut %, relative theoretical maximum). New peptide_qc() lists per peptide state: missing undeuterated control, uptake reported 0 every time (missing reference rather real measurement), negative uptake, FD uptake, theoretical maximum, FD fraction, FD missing / <= 0 / maximum. reports; nothing removed. as_hdx_long() computes default percent deuteration theoretical maximum HDXExaminer DynamX (length - 1 - prolines first residue).

title: HDXBoxeR 0.1.0
text: New read_hdx() reads HDXExaminer “results” tables Waters DynamX cluster state exports (DynamX 2.x 3.x), detecting format header. read_hdxexaminer() read_dynamx() read one format explicitly. DynamX cluster data raw file replicate uptake computed centroid mass; public matched cluster/state data set agrees DynamX’s uptake (r = 0.9999). fd = marks fully deuterated control (control state, state’s last time point); combine_charges = TRUE merges charge states. New as_hdx_long() builds HDXBoxeR input long table exported software, times s, min h. Every function takes filepath now also accepts DynamX file table read_hdx()/as_hdx_long(); reading passing table avoids re-reading file every call.

title: HDXBoxeR 0.1.0
text: output_tp() output_tc() now use every replicate every state default, states may different numbers replicates (e.g. 3 4). Previously states cut smallest count extra replicates silently dropped; replicates = n still caps number. peptide missing measurement kept NA instead dropped, long least min_replicates (new argument, default 2) values every state. Dropped peptides reported. sd_timepoint(), ave_timepoint(), pv_timepoint(), sd_ci_timepoint() pv_timecourse() find state’s replicate columns name ignore missing values; pv_timepoint() returns NA instead failing peptide fewer two values identical replicates. CI_2pts() (CI_tp(), CI_tc() every plot using ) pools state’s SDs weighted degrees freedom uses state’s number replicates. equal, complete replicates result unchanged. results output_tp()/output_tc() record replicates, states, times units attributes. State names matched exactly abbreviations tried, state “WT” longer confused “WT_mut”. output_tc(seq_match = ) now means output_tp() (FALSE: identical sequence required; TRUE: match position). two functions previously used opposite meanings. seq_match = TRUE, output_tp() keeps usual column order (Sequence fourth). compare_states_tp() uses every replicate default (replicates = NULL).

title: HDXBoxeR 0.1.0
text: Robot plots, Woods plots, robot_indexes() robot_indexes_df(): p-values averages came two tables sorted differently (Start text one, number ) combined row row, wrong peptides called significant. also case 0.0.2. tables now order. plots_vol_tp() colors state critical interval instead largest one. plot_heat_map_tp_proc(): default ranges c(-Inf, seq(-30, 30, = 10), Inf), documented (ten times smaller). backHX_calculations() averages replicate centroids peptide calculation, range peptides; state without FD undeuterated data gives NA. output_UD() time-course tables treat missing undeuterated uptake (HDXExaminer n/, DynamX) 0, average_timecourse(), sd_timecourse() _proc versions work data. backHX_calculations() now computes back-exchange measured centroid times charge, (Exp Cent[FD] - Exp Cent[0s]) * Charge. previously used theoretical centroid m/z without charge factor, overstated back-exchange roughly proportion charge state. plot_fissure_vent() (default sd_source = "raw"), interactive plots residue_regions() now build critical interval state’s raw replicate SD, matches CI_tp(), diff_peptides_prep() heat map, Woods robot plots. sd_source = "CI" keeps previous, wider band. critical-interval functions (CI_2pts(), CI_tp(), CI_tc(), CI_single(), compare_timecourse()) use two-tailed t-value, qt(alpha/2, df), HDXBoxeR 0.0.2 Janowska et al. (2024). Multiple-testing correction (p_adjust) uses one family everywhere: peptides one pair states one time point. sd_ci_timepoint() uses correct conversion two-sided interval SD (factor 2 alpha/2). general_info() reports real number replicates.
